title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-33
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 3NT. South has 8 top tricks, 2 spades, the ♥A, the ♦A, and 4 clubs. The ninth trick will have to come from spades. As a diamond shift would be most unwelcome, South should win the ♥A at trick 1.

If spades are 3-3 it will be easy to establish a third spade trick. The correct play gives South an excellent chance to take 3 spade tricks when East has 4 or more spades to the ♠Q and ♠J. The club suit must provide the necessary transportation to the dummy for spade plays. South should begin by cashing the ♣A and overtaking the ♣J or ♣10 in dummy.

When clubs are 3-2, there are enough entries to play spades to best advantage. A small spade is played from dummy. If East plays low, South will win the ♠10. East must therefore split his honors. South wins the ♠K and overtakes his remaining club honor in dummy. A low spade is played towards the ♠10. East wins, blocking the suit, and plays a diamond.

After winning the ♦A, South unblocks the ♠10. South plays his ♣2 to dummy, gaining access to the ♠A.

If clubs are 4-1, South does not have enough dummy entries to pick up long spades with East headed by the ♠Q and ♠J. If West has 4 clubs, there is a reasonable chance he has a singleton spade honor. South should cash the ♠A. If West follows with an honor, South should finesse the ♠10 on the next round.
